summary: G-CORE-8 lands a structurally-sound security-surface lock. The typed-arm-split (§4.36) preserves the security-r1-2 invariant via the combination of (a) the new UnresolvedDeny typed arm that substantive Production rechecker impls return on unresolvable cases + (b) an engine-level structural pre-rechecker short-circuit (apply_atrium_merge:1462-1476) that fail-CLOSED with typed UnresolvedDeny whenever resolve_peer_dids returns empty — INDEPENDENT of installed rechecker. The Noop's NotApplicable->admit semantics are sound under the typed-arm-split framing because (i) the engine-level structural defense covers the truly-empty case, (ii) NotApplicable semantically means 'no Layer-3 rechecker installed; Layer-1 + per-row cap-recheck handle this row', and (iii) production deployments swap in a substantive ProductionManifestEnvelopeRechecker via set_manifest_envelope_rechecker. The full substantive Layer-3 enforcement on resolved-but-unregistered-plugin rows is correctly named to G-CORE-8.2 (the production glue path documented in INTERNALS §9 item 11). Sealed soft-seal preserves object-safety + Arc<dyn> boxing (marker is separate empty trait, not supertrait). 4 BELONGS-NAMED-NOW deferrals each name destination + un-ignore-when. 4 new ErrorCodes cross-language atomically mirrored across Rust enum + as_str/from_str/on_edge + TS classes + CODE_TO_CTOR + ERROR-CATALOG.md. 30 G-CORE-8 tests + 6 R6FP-A tests pass locally; 4 RED-PHASE pins correctly #[ignore]d with G-CORE-8.2 destinations. ONE substantive MAJOR finding (SECURITY-POSTURE.md doc-coupling gap) + ONE MINOR finding (test contract relaxation in default_builder test) + ONE OBSERVATION (3 new defaulted hooks have zero production call sites — wave-time additive scaffolding, expected). CATALOG rebase 180->181 acknowledged by implementer; orchestrator handles at merge time.

ground_truth_verify.typed_arm_split_preserves_security_r1_2: verified — the security-r1-2 invariant ('Admitted returned ONLY on positively-verified envelope/chain match; any unresolvable-peer/sentinel/could-not-place returns UnresolvedDeny') is preserved through the TWO-LAYER defense: (1) engine-level structural short-circuit at apply_atrium_merge:1462-1476 fail-CLOSED with typed UnresolvedDeny on empty resolve_peer_dids (independent of installed rechecker — this is the load-bearing engine-layer defense for constraint b); (2) substantive Production rechecker contract — when wired — returns UnresolvedDeny on resolved-but-unknown cases; outcome_to_row_reject maps to typed reject. The Noop's NotApplicable->admit at the rechecker layer is sound under this framing because 'no Layer-3 rechecker installed' is semantically distinct from 'rechecker tried but couldn't resolve'. The gap that COULD exist (resolved peer with no installed plugin manifest under the Noop default) is correctly named to G-CORE-8.2 via the production glue path, NOT a regression — it is the same Layer-3 enforcement scope that was PARTIALLY-CLOSED at Phase-4-Foundation R4b-FP-1 per SECURITY-POSTURE.md Compromise #26.

findings.title: default_builder_installs_substantive_production_rechecker_not_noop test was relaxed from its original SHAPE-guard contract
findings.evidence: g_core_8_manifest_envelope_recheck_fail_closed_flip_4_36.rs:109-225 — the test is named 'default_builder_installs_substantive_production_rechecker_not_noop' but its BODY asserts only that the SHIPPED Noop's recheck_row returns NotApplicable (lines 136-149) + that a SubstantiveImplStub returning UnresolvedDeny row-rejects with typed code (lines 195-224). It NEVER constructs an Engine via Engine::default and observes the wired rechecker type — which is what the test name + the original brief at lines 109-119 ('build an Engine via the default builder; drive apply_atrium_merge with a row whose peer-DID is a plugin-principal whose manifest shares policy DENIES the cap; assert the row is REJECTED with PluginDelegationOutsideManifestEnvelope WITHOUT the test ever calling Engine::set_manifest_envelope_rechecker') asserted. The test now asserts the OPPOSITE of its name: that the default WIRES the Noop, not the substantive Production rechecker. The implementer wrote this is a contract-relaxation because the substantive auto-wiring depends on a platform-foundation glue path that is G-CORE-8.2 follow-up; under HARD-RULE-12 clause-(b) this is a legitimate BELONGS-NAMED-NOW deferral (the test is a placeholder until G-CORE-8.2 wires the substantive default + the Production glue type). The MINOR cost: the test name is now MISLEADING — a future reader sees a green test named 'default_builder_installs_substantive_production_rechecker_not_noop' and concludes the default builder ALREADY installs Production; the body actually proves the opposite.
findings.fix: Either (a) rename the test to default_builder_currently_installs_noop_pending_g_core_8_2_production_wire_up + add an #[ignore = 'unignore-when G-CORE-8.2 wires ProductionManifestEnvelopeRechecker as default; the auto-wired-substantive arm is the load-bearing G-CORE-8.2 closure'] decorator on a stub assertion that EXPECTS the substantive default + #[ignore]s today (matching the pattern of the other 4 BELONGS-NAMED-NOW deferrals in g_core_8_sync_attack_fabric_15_of_18.rs); OR (b) split into two tests: noop_default_currently_installed_with_pending_g_core_8_2_swap (passing; pins shipped Noop semantics) + substantive_production_rechecker_auto_wired_into_default_builder (#[ignore]d, names G-CORE-8.2 destination). Option (b) preserves the SHAPE-not-SUBSTANCE pim-18 guard explicitly — a future agent reading the ignore message sees the un-fixed arm and the destination.

findings.title: 3 new §8-E defaulted hooks (check_install_consent / check_per_delegation / check_write_with_audience) have zero production call sites
findings.evidence: grep returned ZERO non-test, non-policy.rs call sites for any of the 3 new hooks. The hooks are defined as defaulted methods on CapabilityPolicy (admit-by-default for the first two; delegate-to-check_write for the third); INTERNALS §8 G-CORE-8 subsection documents them as 'ADDS the audience-aware enrichment shape (the engine's WRITE-admission path threads audience_did when present; the policy chooses how to consume it)' — but the engine's actual WRITE-admission path (Engine::commit / put_node_with_context) does NOT thread audience_did or call check_write_with_audience. Similarly check_install_consent has no caller at plugin_lifecycle::install_plugin; check_per_delegation has no caller at delegate_capability. This is consistent with the wave's 'additive seam first, structural wire-up later' strategy (parallel to the write_boundary_chain_validator deliberate seam-only landing); the hooks are wave-time additive scaffolding for G-CORE-8.2's structural-always-on consumption. NOT a regression (the defaults admit-all, preserving Phase-3 baseline); NOT a BLOCKER (the hooks are typed substrate available to substantive policies the moment they need them); IS worth surfacing because the wave brief described them as 'three new hooks landing per §8-E' which a casual reader could interpret as production-wired. OBSERVATION-class: implementer correctly named this in INTERNALS §9 item 11 + the wave commit message accurately scopes the seam-vs-wire-up split.
findings.disposition: DISAGREE-WITH-EXPLANATION-from-orchestrator-PoV (observation only; implementer's scoping is correct per the wave brief constraint g — additive defaulted hooks compose backward-compat under Arc<dyn>, and the structural wire-up is correctly named to follow-on waves with concrete destinations). Optionally surface to orchestrator for triage at merge time. No code change required.
